newsitem.title: QATAR: Abu Dhabi owns two-thirds of Gulf Air - official.
newsitem.headline: Abu Dhabi owns two-thirds of Gulf Air - official.

text.p: Abu Dhabi has increased its stake in loss-making regional carrier Gulf Air to around two-thirds from an original 25 percent, but it does not plan to take over the airline, Gulf officials said on Monday.
They did not say when the increase took place nor what the shareholding of the carrier's three other owners now was.
"There are varying and conflicting ways of calculating ownership, but you can say that Abu Dhabi holds a two-thirds stake," one official said.

Speaking on the sidelines of a Gulf Cooperation Council summit, officials said Abu Dhabi -- which set up Gulf Air in equal participation with Qatar, Oman and Bahrain -- had considered taking control of the airline.
But it decided against the move and against plans to shift the carrier's headquarters from Manama to the UAE capital Abu Dhabi to protect jobs in Bahrain, another official said.
Unemployment in Bahrain, the least wealthy Gulf Arab state, has fanned unrest among members of its Shi'ite Moslem community demanding political and economic reforms.
Gulf Air suffered losses of $159 million last year.
